chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Fifteen-dollar whiskey and a drunken trumpeter
summary: Kirby bought bar whiskey instead of using the shop next door, and a fresh bottle came every set until the trumpet player nearly fell off the stand.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Anyway, they got a room back there which was our room, you know. So he's walking me towards the front door. And I thought he was going next door to the whiskey store to get a bottle of whiskey. But instead, he walks over to the bar in the place, and orders a bottle of whiskey from the bar, when all he had to do was walk out of the front door, and right next door was the whiskey store -- right directly next door! And whiskey in Washington is very cheap; and of course, in a nightclub, they charge anything they want. Because the whiskey we ordered at the time, I mean, it was a cheap whiskey, it would run about six or seven dollars, I guess, or something like that. And Kirby, he goes to the bar: Give me a fifth of whiskey." The bartender said, "Fifteen dollars." He paid it and (?) like it wasn't nothin'. I said, "Kirby, that don't make sense. You walk right out the door, you're in the whiskey store. Why spend that much money for a bottle of whiskey? It's no trouble going in the
whiskey store." "Don't worry about a thing. Don't worry about a thing."

We go back to our little room, and Wallace Bishop, the drummer, he had taken the bottle out of Kirby's hand and opened it up, poured out a big water glass full of whiskey, Billy Kyle got his, and by the time the bottle got back around to me, there was a little bit in there -- but they really emptied that bottle. And they're drinkin' and talkin'. After all, this is my first night on the job, you know. I don't know nothin' about the different temperaments in the band. I've got to watch that whiskey.

So anyway, when we went back on the stand, that bottle was empty. When we come off the next time, Kirby had another bottle! He ordered another bottle. Well, now they're gettin' down with it pretty good. I'm drinkin' along with 'em! I feel real good now. All right. This is the way I like to work. You know, I feel good. And everybody's feelin' good...

The trumpet player went to stand up to play his solo, and almost fell off the stand. I had to grab him to keep him from fallin' off the front of the stand. So he set him back down, and he blew his solo sitting down.
So anyway, we finished that set, we go up, we come back... Kirby had another bottle! Every time we went off
the stand, we'd have another bottle of whiskey. Well, the band was pretty high that night. It was really high.

But like I say, Kirby, he still taken me home where I was living, taking me in a cab, and still talking about the raise I got coming -- which he had given. Oh, he was very generous. And he asked me was there anything else I wanted to needed or this-that-and-the-other. Buttering up somebody... He really buttered me up. But he was all right to work with.
And later, we come back to New York after we had finished the engagement. We were there like two weeks, I think...
